claims.text: In the APSO reading version as amended by the12th amending statute, §22(1) says attempting to influence an examination result through deception or unauthorized aids leads to a failing grade. Suitable software may check unacknowledged text or sources, while the examiner determines whether deception occurred. Under §22(2), disruption may lead to exclusion from that examination and a failing grade. In serious or repeated deception or disruption cases, the examination committee may exclude the student from further examinations in the degree program, with final failure of the degree examination (§22(3)). Under §24(6), an examination failed because of §22 deception or disruption may be retaken only once. These are general examination provisions, not a separate AI-specific sanction schedule.

claims.text: The Guidelines for Writing Theses and Seminar Papers (Juli 2026) issued by the TUM Chair of Marketing and Consumer Research permit the use of generative AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity) as research aids for seminar, Bachelor's, and Master's theses, subject to mandatory declaration inserted before the bibliography. The declaration requires students to specify the exact tools used and the specific tasks performed (brainstorming, literature search, structuring, code generation, hypothesis generation, translation, image generation, or language improvement), and confirm that they personally reviewed the entire thesis and accept full responsibility. If no AI tools were used, a formal non-use statement must be included ('Ich habe keine generativen KI-Tools oder -Hilfsmittel verwendet.'). AI-generated images must cite the specific tool, and the use of AI for empirical data collection and analysis is prohibited for data protection reasons unless explicitly approved by the thesis supervisor. These are the reviewed chair guidelines; no broader TUM rule established.

topics.title: 隐私与敏感数据
topics.summary: TUM ProLehre guidance instructs students and instructors not to enter personal, sensitive, or confidential data into AI tools, which applies also to TUM-approved systems. In addition, teaching and study materials (such as lecture slides, scripts, recordings, or past exams) are protected intellectual property and require explicit instructor consent before being uploaded to or processed in AI tools, even when used solely for personal study purposes like summarization, transcription, or translation.
topics.scope: TUM ProLehre 教学指引；APSO 第 12 次修订规程阅读整理本（最新登载修订 2025 年 12 月 16 日；正式公布规程具法定效力）；SGwP 科研规范条例；MKT 教席论文规范。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

claims.text: TUM ProLehre guidance instructs students and instructors not to enter personal, sensitive, or confidential data into AI tools, including systems approved by TUM. Prohibited categories include names, matriculation numbers, email addresses, patient records, research participant data, exam data, and confidential research results. Users are instructed to anonymize content prior to entry, utilize generalized or neutral sample texts, and consult instructors or the TUM Data Protection Officer when uncertain.

evidence.quote: Geben Sie keine personenbezogenen, sensiblen oder vertraulichen Daten in KI-Tools ein – auch nicht in von der TUM freigegebene Systeme.

topics.summary: TUM SGwP statutes establish research integrity standards requiring research data retention on durable secure media, ordinarily for 10 years from publication unless justified shorter periods or discipline-specific standards apply. Guidelines from the MKT Chair permit AI as a research aid for theses but prohibit AI empirical data collection and analysis unless explicitly approved by the supervisor.

claims.text: The reviewed TUM-SGwP statute requires researchers working at TUM to follow recognized scientific standards, document work, question results and act honestly (§1). Supervisors must verifiably give the statute to students conducting scientific thesis work (§22). Under §8, primary and evaluated data and evaluation software used for publications must be kept on durable secure media in the originating institution; retention depends on discipline and is ordinarily ten years from the relevant publication, with reasons for non-retention or shorter periods documented. Authorship requires a genuine, traceable contribution and honorary authorship is prohibited (§12). Under §13, scientific misconduct involves knowingly or grossly negligently making false statements, violating others' intellectual property or impairing their research in a scientifically relevant context. Anyone may approach the ombudsperson concerning suspected misconduct (§16).

claims.text: The Guidelines for Writing Theses and Seminar Papers (Juli 2026) issued by the TUM Chair of Marketing and Consumer Research permit the use of generative AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity) as research aids for seminar, Bachelor's, and Master's theses, subject to mandatory declaration inserted before the bibliography. The declaration requires students to specify the exact tools used and the specific tasks performed (brainstorming, literature search, structuring, code generation, hypothesis generation, translation, image generation, or language improvement), and confirm that they personally reviewed the entire thesis and accept full responsibility. If no AI tools were used, a formal non-use statement must be included ('Ich habe keine generativen KI-Tools oder -Hilfsmittel verwendet.'). AI-generated images must cite the specific tool, and the use of AI for empirical data collection and analysis is prohibited for data protection reasons unless explicitly approved by the thesis supervisor. These are the reviewed chair guidelines; no broader TUM rule established.

additionalTopics.title: 学术诚信与纪律程序
additionalTopics.summary: Under the reviewed APSO reading version, attempted deception in examinations or coursework results in an assessment grade of 5.0 (fail). A failed examination resulting from deception or disruption may be retaken only once under § 24(6). Under § 25(3), a candidate may inspect examination files upon reasoned written application to the examination board chair within 1 month of grade announcement, with time and place determined by the chair with the examiner. Under § 21, procedural defects must be raised promptly in writing. Formally published enactments remain legally authoritative over the reading consolidation. The inspection window is not a deadline for disciplinary or administrative appeals, which remain unreviewed.
additionalTopics.scope: TUM ProLehre 教学指引；APSO 第 12 次修订规程阅读整理本（最新登载修订 2025 年 12 月 16 日；正式公布规程具法定效力）；SGwP 科研规范条例；MKT 教席论文规范。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

claims.text: In the APSO reading version as amended by the12th amending statute, §22(1) says attempting to influence an examination result through deception or unauthorized aids leads to a failing grade. Suitable software may check unacknowledged text or sources, while the examiner determines whether deception occurred. Under §22(2), disruption may lead to exclusion from that examination and a failing grade. In serious or repeated deception or disruption cases, the examination committee may exclude the student from further examinations in the degree program, with final failure of the degree examination (§22(3)). Under §24(6), an examination failed because of §22 deception or disruption may be retaken only once. These are general examination provisions, not a separate AI-specific sanction schedule.

claims.text: In the reviewed APSO reading version, §25(3) grants access to written examination work, examiner reports and oral-examination minutes on a reasoned written application after results are announced. The application must reach the examination committee chair within one month of announcement; the chair determines the time and place with the examiner. Under §21, examination-procedure defects must be raised promptly in writing to the committee chair or examiner. This inspection window does not establish a deadline for disciplinary or administrative appeals, which remain unreviewed.
